clue.text: Behind back cloth, long to make entrance

indicators.note: behind places the word for long after the turned cloth in the answer
back tells us the word for cloth is to be read from its end to its start

parts.note: cloth woven as a web, a piece of fabric
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to make a grand stage entrance from behind the backcloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb, stressed on the second syllable, meaning to enchant, not a doorway; the surface's theatrical backcloth hides the 'back' reversal indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to cast a spell over them, to enchant.

clue.text: After big cut,'series held in tandem perhaps

indicators.note: after puts the word for series behind the shortened word
cut means the word big loses its tail

parts.note: taken as written
a cycle is a series, of songs or events

explanation.surface: A major series held on a two-seater after a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandem is one example of a two-wheeled pedal machine.

clue.text: Don Juan: wise man or lunatic?

indicators.note: lunatic means the letters are mad, rearranged wildly

explanation.surface: Is the legendary seducer a sage or a madman?
explanation.definitionFit: Don Juan is the archetypal seducer, a habitual chaser of women.

clue.text: Diplomacy secures right to piece of land

indicators.note: secures means the word for diplomacy holds the letter inside it

parts.note: tact is diplomacy

explanation.surface: Diplomatic skill wins the rights to some territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is an expanse or area of land.

clue.text: Sort of boots a tramp nearly succeeded in getting hold of

indicators.note: nearly means the word for tramp is cut short of its final letter

parts.note: a hobo is a tramp
to nail someone is to catch them

explanation.surface: A tramp almost managed to grab some boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobnailed boots are heavy footwear studded with short nails, so the word describes a kind of boot.

clue.text: Ways to hold us back bodily

indicators.note: back tells us the whole assembled run is read in the opposite direction
to hold means the word for ways takes the next word inside it

parts.note: lanes are ways or roads
taken as written

explanation.surface: Roads seem to restrain us physically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' governs everything before it, so the container is built first and only then turned round; 'bodily' is the definition, as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensual pleasures are those of the body, physical rather than intellectual.

clue.text: Instrument playing one of the blues

parts.note: the sax is a musical instrument
on means playing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: An instrument performing a blues number.
explanation.walkthrough: Saxon blue is a shade of blue, not a musical blues.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxon blue is a shade, so the word names a type of blue colour.

clue.text: Paragon will be in dire peril anon

indicators.note: dire signals the letters are in a terrible state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A model of virtue is soon going to be in grave danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonpareil is a person or thing without equal, a model of excellence.

clue.text: An old book is so unreadable

definitions.text: An old book is so unreadable

parts.words: An old book is so unreadable
parts.note: old books were sold with their page edges still joined, which had to be slit open before reading

explanation.surface: A complaint that an antique volume is illegible.
explanation.definitionFit: A book with folded pages not yet slit apart cannot be read until a knife is used.

clue.text: Vocabulary' of Roman law, something much admired

parts.note: lex is the Latin word for law
an icon is an object of great admiration

explanation.surface: The terminology of Roman law, a widely revered thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is a dictionary or a word stock of a language.

clue.text: Stop being a butterfly

explanation.surface: Someone halts while pretending to be an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark that marks a pause in a sentence, and a European butterfly named for the white mark on its wing.

clue.text: Take turns at two sports?

explanation.surface: An invitation to alternate between playing two games.
explanation.walkthrough: Box and Cox are characters in a Victorian farce who share a room in shifts, never meeting; boxing and coxing a rowing boat are the two sports.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes two people alternating in a role, and boxing plus coxing a rowing crew are both sporting activities.

clue.text: Force to study and overwork

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
to strain is to overwork or overtax

explanation.surface: A student is pushed to study and work too hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to compel or oblige them.

clue.text: Classically simple room

explanation.surface: A plain room in the classical style.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic describes the elegant, simple style of ancient Athens, and it is also a loft room beneath the roof.

clue.text: Result when opponents go to law

parts.note: East and North are opposing partnerships at bridge, abbreviated E and N
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: What happens when two rivals end up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play East-West, so any East and North pair are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a consequence, a verb like the definition.

clue.text: 'After return, was carried from terminal

indicators.note: after places the word for was carried behind the word for return

parts.note: to return a candidate is to elect them
rode means travelled as a passenger, was carried

explanation.surface: After coming back, someone was transported from the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal' is not a station but an electrical contact; 'return' means elect, as voters return an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a conductor through which current enters or leaves, an electrical terminal.

clue.text: Kittens, say, born in wastepaper basket

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals, kittens being one example
taken as written

explanation.surface: Newborn kittens are found in a bin for waste paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle for rubbish in the street or office, the same kind of thing as a wastepaper basket.

clue.text: Canvas sheet physicist dipped in water

indicators.note: dipped in means the scientist is placed inside the word for water

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
Wolfgang Pauli was an Austrian physicist

explanation.surface: A scientist dunked a canvas sheet in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy waterproof cover, often canvas.

clue.text: Hurry off, due to translate a verse from Matthew

parts.note: beat it means go away quickly

indicators.note: to translate signals the letters of due are converted into a new order

explanation.surface: Rushing off to translate a Bible verse in time.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatitudes are the blessings in the Sermon on the Mount in Matthew's gospel, each one verse.

clue.text: Forbid money to servant

parts.note: to bar is to prohibit
legal tender is money

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to pay a domestic servant.
explanation.definitionFit: One who serves drinks at a bar, so a servant of customers.

clue.text: Deputise for absent principals over dormant issue

definitions.text: Deputise for absent principals over dormant issue

parts.words: Deputise for absent principals over dormant issue
parts.note: standing in for parents who are out, sitting watch over a sleeping child, 'issue' meaning offspring

explanation.surface: Stand in for missing bosses while a dormant matter waits.
explanation.definitionFit: Minding a sleeping child while the parents are out is exactly this job.

clue.text: Goes first to the roof

explanation.surface: Someone heads up to the roof before anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead is to go in front, and lead sheets covering a roof are known collectively by this plural.

clue.text: Hunt, in a way, displays trickery

indicators.note: in places the poet's first name inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for street, a way
Leigh Hunt was an English Romantic poet and essayist

explanation.surface: Hunting, in a sense, shows cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt' is the poet Leigh Hunt, so it yields his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is dexterity used to deceive, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Ideal cage for a wild animal

indicators.note: cage for means the word for ideal encloses the following letter like bars

parts.note: the best is the ideal, the perfect
taken as written

explanation.surface: The perfect enclosure for a wild creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is a creature, especially a large or fierce one.

clue.text: Girl can be 'such a fool

explanation.surface: A young woman can be very silly.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, and an April fool is someone tricked on the first day of that month.

clue.text: It may be right to sell citizenship

definitions.text: It may be right to sell

explanation.surface: Selling citizenship might be the proper thing.
explanation.walkthrough: A franchise is a right granted to sell a company's goods, and also the right to vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence granted to trade a brand's goods, and the vote or full civic rights.

clue.text: Sneak in first, as the New Yorkers say?

indicators.note: the Brooklyn accent famously pronounces the ir sound as oi

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting in early, in Brooklyn style.
explanation.definitionFit: To foist something is to slip it in or impose it surreptitiously.

clue.text: Many predatory birds have hoods

parts.note: c is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
owls are birds of prey

explanation.surface: Lots of birds of prey wear hoods.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowls are monks' hoods.

clue.text: Tar sailor spilled about suit

indicators.note: spilled suggests the letters are knocked over and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor knocks something over on his suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' is a sailor in the surface, but here it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartorial means relating to tailoring and clothes, such as a suit.

clue.text: Wife sounded distressed

parts.note: a bell rung has sounded

explanation.surface: A wife sounded upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrung heart is one tormented or anguished.

annotationWithheld.clue: Every German in, the race was very boastful

clue.text: Promotion at last: the rise is beginning

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word promotion

parts.note: an ascent is a rise

explanation.surface: Finally promoted, someone's career is starting to take off.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means coming into being, just starting to develop.
